title: Smoked Salmon Kedgeree
subtitle: Basmati rice with smoked salmon, eggs, and dill
excerpt: Basmati rice spiced with curry powder, folded with flakes of smoked salmon, soft-boiled eggs, and fresh dill. A quick, elegant version of the traditional kedgeree.

recipe.sourceNotes: This is a modern variation on the traditional kedgeree, which uses smoked haddock. Smoked salmon gives a quicker-cooking, less intensely smoky result, and the dish can be assembled in under 30 minutes without poaching fish in milk. The spicing stays true to the Anglo-Indian original: curry powder, butter, and lemon. The combination of cold smoked salmon and warm spiced rice creates a pleasant contrast of temperatures in the finished dish.

content.text: Cook the rice by the absorption method for the most reliably fluffy result. Let the rice steam off the heat after cooking rather than lifting the lid. Fold the smoked salmon in at the last moment off the heat so it barely warms through rather than cooks: overheated smoked salmon turns rubbery.
Cook the eggs: bring a pan of water to the boil, lower in the eggs, and cook for 7 minutes. Drain and run under cold water. Peel and halve.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the curry powder, turmeric, and bay leaves. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed rice and 500 ml cold water. Season. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Remove from heat and leave undisturbed for 5 minutes.

Discard the bay leaves. Fluff the rice with a fork. Add the lemon zest, lemon juice, and most of the dill. Fold in the smoked salmon off the heat. Divide into bowls. Top with the halved eggs and remaining dill.
